# RedTeam Update: Why We Went Quiet, What We Built, and Where We're Going

**Source:** RedTeam @_redteam_ on X · Feb 12 (passed to Subnet Magazine on 2026-05-16 by Rondo)
**Subnet:** SN61 RedTeam · Commercial vehicle: Innerworks · http://theredteam.io
**Tone:** Team self-report on commercial breakout, technical roadmap, and a novel token-economic commitment

---

## Section 1 · Commercial breakout

**Premise.** RedTeam (SN61) exists to solve "a new paradigm in cybersecurity, one where attacks are generated by AI agents, evolve autonomously, and outpace every traditional defence on the market." The subnet is the research engine. Innerworks is the commercial vehicle that takes that research to market.

### Customers and integrations the team disclosed

- **Major global messaging platform** (name to be revealed): Innerworks now fully integrated across the platform and its wider ecosystem. Device intelligence, bot detection, true geolocation. **100M+ daily active users**. Explicitly NOT a pilot or PoC — this is "live, in production, at a scale that most cybersecurity companies will never touch."
- **1inch** (leading DeFi ecosystem): paying customer using the full stack (device fingerprinting, bot detection, geolocation). Recently announced partnership.
- **In pipeline or active PoC**: DEXs, protocols, transaction monitoring platforms (traditional and crypto), payment providers, identity verification tools.

### The team's positioning vs incumbents

> "Traditional cybersecurity companies run multi-month red team audits. By the time they identify vulnerabilities and deploy fixes, the threat landscape has already shifted. Their detection capabilities fragment over time until they effectively don't work. This has gotten dramatically worse with the rise of agentic attack generation.
>
> Our approach is fundamentally different. RedTeam miners are constantly probing, breaking, and innovating, and their output flows directly into Innerworks' production systems. This methodology is why we're winning contracts against billion-dollar incumbents. We didn't outspend them. We out-innovated them by leveraging decentralised R&D at a pace no traditional team can match."

### The R&D-budget-to-Alpha-buyback commitment (this is the novel part)

Innerworks is structurally committing R&D budget to flow directly into Alpha buybacks rather than into a centralized internal team.

- **Starts at baseline 1 TAO/day**.
- Additional buybacks as injection when big milestones hit.
- Framing: "the subnet and its miners as key stakeholders in the company. Not an afterthought. Not a side channel."
- Explicitly NOT a revenue-share or percentage of SaaS. A committed R&D budget.
- Self-aware on the small starting number: "If the company is growing this fast, why start at 1 TAO/day? Because this is the beginning of a model, not the end of it. We want to iterate on this carefully and set a standard we can consistently grow from."
- Trajectory: "constant and considerable increases" as commercial milestones land.

---

## Section 2 · The future, "the internet's first immune system"

The vision the team is shipping toward, biological-immune-system framing throughout.

### What they have built already

> "Over the past 6 months, we've developed an internal immune system agent. This system analyses attacks coming through the subnet, reverse-engineers the methods, generates countermeasures, and proposes them directly to our engineers for review and deployment. What used to take weeks of manual reverse engineering now takes hours."

### Where they are going

> "The next phase is incentivising miners to build adaptive attack agents. Think of them as digital viruses. These agents don't just submit static scripts. They continuously adapt and evolve until they can bypass proposed challenges. On the other side, our immune system agent analyses these attacks in real-time, generates defences, and deploys them back into production for the attack agents to test again.
>
> The biological analogy is exact: antigens (miner attack agents) trigger antibody production (automated defences), which get deployed and remembered by the system. The viruses mutate. The immune system adapts. The cycle repeats, entirely on machine time."

## Section 3 · Technical detail (substantial)

### Version history
- **v1.0.0**: adversarial challenges, Humanise Behaviour challenge, script uniqueness checking, challenge CI/CD, centralised + local scoring, validator-miner commit tracking, resource limits
- **v2.0.0**: operational stability, auto-updater for validators, domain migration to theredteam.io, hotfixes for commit-related issues
- **v3.0.0**: redefined challenge architecture, Auto Browser Sniffer + new modular structure
- **v4.0.0**: monorepo split into focused repos (validators, miners, scoring server), restructured configurations, updated full lifecycle documentation

### Repository scale
- 46 repositories across the RedTeamSubnet org
- 2,000+ commits
- 26 releases

### Active challenges (2 of 14 still live; 9 deprecated because miners solved most cases or submissions converged)
- **Auto Browser Sniffer (AB Sniffer)**: miners build SDKs that detect/identify automation frameworks by name, across headless and headed-but-silent modes. Submission scale: **v1 had 4 accepted commits, v4 has 105 (about 28x growth)**.
- **Anti-Detect Automation Detection (AAD)**: detect browser automation running inside anti-detect browsers where static signals are masked and fingerprints are fresh. Detection relies on runtime behaviour and orchestration patterns.

### Scoring system, four iterations
1. **Winner-takes-all**: only the top submission rewarded. Killed miner retention.
2. **Softmax-based distribution**: proportional rewards across multiple miners.
3. **Time-based decay with stability windows**: submissions earn full rewards for 10 days, decay over days 10-15, fully expire after day 15. Miners must beat their own previous best to refresh. Similarity checks catch copying.
4. **Filtering, similarity penalties, de-duplication**: strict acceptance criteria, similarity-based score adjustments, automatic grouping of miners by Axon/coldkey to prevent gaming with multiple UIDs.

### Infrastructure highlights
- Centralised scoring system addresses weight divergence among validators, reduces compute costs
- Multi-layer isolation to protect against malicious miner submissions
- Containerised deployment
- RedTeam Analyser: categorises and extracts methods from each submission, calculates incentives and burns, tracks miner achievements through dedicated UI
- Dashboard has separate miner/validator views, submission lifecycle tracking, score decay visualisation, similarity analysis with comparison logs, detailed submission introspection

### Coming Feb 14 (likely already shipped by May)
- ADA v2 with hardened browser-level obfuscation via NSTBrowser + new fail-fast scoring architecture
- Removal of the reveal interval (no longer serving its purpose)
- Migration from MongoDB to a relational database
- Option for miners to submit solutions from private DockerHub repositories (to protect their code)

## Desk notes on provenance and the angles the Oracle should engage

- **Article is Feb 12 2026** but passed through to the desk on May 16. The desk should verify whether the messaging platform name has since been disclosed publicly, whether the 1 TAO/day baseline has scaled, and whether ADA v2 + the MongoDB migration shipped on schedule.

- **The 1 TAO/day starting figure is small but the MODEL is the story.** At current TAO prices (call it ~$300 for round numbers), 1 TAO/day is ~$300/day of buyback pressure. The interesting fact is NOT the magnitude, it is that a Bittensor subnet's commercial vehicle has formally committed to a fixed R&D budget allocation that flows directly into the alpha token. This pattern is emerging across multiple subnets simultaneously:
  - Lium (SN51): per the morning's @taomedia_ tip, buybacks "from credit revenue" with a publicly tweeted >$150K burn on May 3
  - RedTeam (SN61): 1 TAO/day baseline + milestone-triggered injections
  - Vanta (SN8) per the WallStreetBets thesis: "fees are used to buy back alpha tokens, creating a direct flywheel"
  - This is a worth-tracking ECOSYSTEM PATTERN, not a one-off

- **The biological immune system framing is unusually good editorial material.** The antibody/antigen loop running "entirely on machine time" is a quotable mechanism description. The Oracle should engage with it on the merits but also flag the open question: when the attack agents and defense agents both evolve via the same training mechanism, what stops the equilibrium from converging on a stalemate where neither side gains ground? This is the structural risk the team has not addressed in the post.

- **100M+ DAU messaging integration is a HUGE claim.** Confirming the name is the most valuable single follow-up; only a handful of platforms hit that scale (Telegram, WhatsApp, WeChat, Line, KakaoTalk, Viber, Signal at the high end of credible). Worth pressing on at the next opportunity.

- **The 28x growth in AB Sniffer submission quality (4 to 105 across v1 to v4)** is a clean defensible quantitative claim and a strong illustration of the "decentralized R&D at a pace no traditional team can match" thesis.

- **Comparison angle the Oracle should consider:** RedTeam SN61 vs Score SN44 (computer vision, PwC partnership). Both are subnets that have moved past "interesting research" into "real enterprise contracts." Their go-to-market structures differ (Score signed a Big Four distribution alliance, RedTeam built a direct commercial vehicle in Innerworks). A future Oracle Subnet Spotlight comparing the two commercialization paths would be high-value editorial.
